description: Jonathan Dooley at New Mexico Institute of Mining and Technology publishes a minimal working example for removing background methane or ethane from measurements collected with a UAV-mounted MIRA Pico sensor. The August 2024 Zenodo software archive and GitHub repository are free under GPL 3.0. Python code accepts timestamps and CH4 or C2H6 columns, smooths and segments readings, filters gradients and outliers, and returns an estimated background and adjusted concentrations. It also retains intermediate masks and diagnostic fields. The routine can prepare local industrial, landfill or wastewater plume observations for emission-transport simulations. Geographic coverage depends on the supplied flight data. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this code. It was developed with Python 3.11 and documents NumPy, pandas and Matplotlib dependencies. Filter settings may require dataset-specific changes, so automatic transfer is uncertain. Code execution and effects of background choices on flux estimates were not independently assessed.
